Per CyrusOne's own facility materials and an aggregator listing dedicated to this specific building, PHX1 sits at 2305-2335 South Ellis Street, Chandler, AZ 85286, part of CyrusOne's roughly 2,000,000 sq ft, eight-building Chandler campus (PHX1 through PHX8) totaling a publicly stated 169 MW of IT capacity across the whole campus; that campus-wide MW figure is not confirmed as this individual building's own capacity, so it is not asserted here as a single-building number.

profile.campus: Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona (CyrusOne Phoenix-metro campus, PHX1-PHX8)
profile.address: 2305 South Ellis Street, Building 5, Chandler, AZ 85286
profile.reading:
CyrusOne PHX3 is Building 5 on CyrusOne's Chandler, Arizona campus, addressed at 2305 South Ellis Street, Chandler, AZ 85286. It is one of eight buildings on a single roughly 2,000,000 square foot campus, numbered PHX1 through PHX8, that CyrusOne states carries 169 MW of power capacity in total. That combined figure describes the whole eight-building site, not any one building on it, and CyrusOne has not published a separate megawatt or square footage figure for PHX3 beyond what trade press reported when the building broke ground.

The Chandler campus grew in phases starting in the early 2010s. CyrusOne's own materials and Data Center Knowledge's coverage from that period describe PHX1 opening in February 2013 with roughly 150,000 square feet of shell space and about 80,000 square feet of operational data center space at 28 MW, and PHX2 following in 2014 at a smaller scale, roughly 60,000 square feet of shell holding about 35,000 square feet of data center space at 6 MW. PHX3 itself broke ground in June 2015 with a planned 120,000 square foot shell, and the same report noted CyrusOne had not yet set the building's final power allocation at that stage. No later figure specific to PHX3 has been found, so none is recorded here.

Design standards published for the whole campus include a TIA 942 Class 4 rating, described as capable of exceeding 1,000 watts per square foot of usable floor, and a 36 inch raised floor system. Certification claims vary across the eight buildings. PHX3 holds Energy Star Data Center Certification individually, and falls within the PHX1 through PHX5 group that holds Green Globe Three Globes certification. NWF Certified Wildlife Habitat status covers all eight buildings on the campus, PHX1 through PHX8.

CyrusOne itself has changed hands several times. Dave Ferdman founded the company in Texas in 2000 as a high density colocation provider for energy sector customers in Houston and Dallas. Private equity firm ABRY Partners bought the company in 2007, and Cincinnati Bell acquired it for 525 million dollars in 2010. Cincinnati Bell then spun CyrusOne off as a public real estate investment trust through a January 2013 initial public offering. The public company grew for nearly a decade until 2022, when investment firms KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners took it private again in an all cash deal. Shareholders were paid 90.50 dollars per share, a premium of about 2.5 percent to the prior closing price, and the deal was valued near 15 billion dollars including assumed debt. The two firms announced the transaction closed on March 25, 2022.

CyrusOne today is headquartered at 2850 North Harwood Street in Dallas and describes its current footprint as more than 60 data centers across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia Pacific, up from the roughly 40 facilities and 4 million square feet the company reported around the time of the take private deal. Its business is wholesale and colocation, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale customers rather than operating its own end user cloud service, the same model followed by peers such as Digital Realty and QTS.

The Chandler campus sits in the Phoenix metro, one of the larger secondary United States data center markets, a status trade press attributes partly to electricity costs below California and the Pacific Northwest, Arizona's comparatively low natural disaster exposure with limited seismic activity and no hurricane risk, and state tax treatment for data center equipment. Eight buildings on one site sharing one utility connection give CyrusOne flexibility to lease Chandler capacity to multiple tenants at different scales, from smaller colocation footprints up to larger blocks, though nothing published here indicates PHX3 specifically is configured for large single tenant AI training clusters rather than general multi tenant colocation.

This building at 2725 Bilter Road in Aurora, Illinois is the third data center CyrusOne added to its original Aurora campus, and the company's own materials group it with its two neighbors as CHI1, CHI2, and CHI3. The campus's history is unusually well documented because CyrusOne was a publicly traded real estate investment trust for most of the period this campus was built, and its SEC filings record that CyrusOne acquired the original 428,000 square foot Aurora facility, now CHI1, on March 31, 2016, for approximately 131.1 million dollars including transaction costs, and that CME Group, parent of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, signed a 15 year lease for data center space in that building effective April 1, 2016, one of the anchor tenancies that shaped this campus's early identity. The same SEC disclosure notes CyrusOne acquired roughly 15 acres of adjacent land at the same time for future development. A second building, CHI2, was added to the site in 2017. This building, CHI3, was added to the site in 2023, according to later trade press describing the campus's history in the context of CyrusOne's subsequent Aurora expansion plans.

CyrusOne's current marketing page for this campus states the site totals 16 acres and 450,000 square feet of technical IT space, with 114 megawatts of total IT capacity across all three buildings, cabinet capacity up to 17 kilowatts, and 98 percent carbon free or renewable electricity. It also states Green Globe three globes certification, but attributes that certification specifically to CHI1 and CHI2, not to CHI3, so this building's own certification status is not confirmed here. No source found in this research session breaks the 450,000 square feet or 114 megawatts down building by building, so none of that campus total is assigned to CHI3 individually, and this building's own square footage, IT critical load, utility feed, standby generation, or onsite generation are not separately disclosed by CyrusOne in any source located.

CyrusOne's presence in the Aurora area has grown well beyond this three building campus since CHI3 was added. Separately, in June 2024 the Yorkville Planning and Zoning Commission in neighboring Kendall County recommended rezoning roughly 230 acres from single family residential to general manufacturing for a still larger, longer horizon CyrusOne campus of up to nine two story buildings planned over 10 to 20 years, a proposal that drew stated resident concern over construction and noise. Both of those newer projects sit in the same Aurora area corridor as CHI3 and illustrate the pace of CyrusOne's regional growth, but neither is this building, and neither project's figures are attributed to CHI3 here. No Aurora Planning and Zoning Commission item specifically authorizing this building's 2023 construction was located and confirmed in this research session, a gap left open rather than guessed at.

CyrusOne operates its Somerset, New Jersey data center, branded NYM1, in Franklin Township within Somerset County, part of the New York metropolitan area's New Jersey data center corridor along the Interstate 287 technology belt. The facility gives CyrusOne a presence in one of the busiest markets on the US East Coast for financial services, telecommunications, and enterprise colocation demand, serving customers who need proximity to the New York and northern New Jersey business core without the real estate costs of a Manhattan location.

NYM1 is a substantial wholesale and colocation facility. CyrusOne's own published specifications put the site at more than 430,000 square feet at full build, with 185,000 square feet of technical, revenue generating data center space and 23 megawatts of total IT capacity available to customers. The facility is built to a Tier III plus design with N+2 redundancy on its critical power and cooling infrastructure, meaning it maintains two additional units of backup capacity beyond what is needed to run the facility at full load, a level of redundancy aimed at large enterprise and hyperscale tenants with stringent uptime requirements. The building has also earned LEED Gold certification under the Core and Shell rating system, reflecting sustainable design choices in its base building construction, structural systems, and building envelope.

CyrusOne, founded in 2001 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas, operates a global portfolio of data centers spanning North America, Europe, and South America, serving hyperscale cloud providers, enterprise customers, and other large scale tenants that need substantial, dedicated power and space commitments rather than smaller colocation cabinets. The Somerset facility fits that broader company profile as a wholesale style campus built for large power dense deployments rather than a small multi tenant colocation shop.

New Jersey's data center market, anchored by Somerset County alongside other established colocation hubs elsewhere in the state, has grown steadily as demand for cloud infrastructure and enterprise IT capacity near New York City has outpaced availability in denser, more expensive parts of the metropolitan area, a dynamic that has drawn wholesale operators like CyrusOne to invest in large scale campuses in the New Jersey suburbs rather than the city core itself. As is standard for wholesale data center operators serving large corporate and hyperscale clients, CyrusOne does not publicly disclose the specific identities of tenants occupying capacity at the Somerset facility, consistent with confidentiality practices across the data center industry for major customer deployments.

reading:
CyrusOne was founded in 2000 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas. KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners completed a take-private acquisition of the company in March 2022 for approximately $15 billion, and it is no longer an independent SEC filer, its prior public CIK, 1553023, now covers only historical pre-acquisition filings.

The company's own site describes its portfolio only in round terms, more than 50 high-performance mission-critical facilities worldwide, while a secondary Wikipedia summary puts the figure at over 40 carrier-neutral data centers across North America, Europe, and Asia. Neither source gives a precise current count, a megawatt capacity total, or a dollar-denominated construction investment figure, so this entry cannot state CyrusOne's exact global or US facility count with confidence beyond these two approximate, disagreeing ranges.

The registry here tracks 47 CyrusOne facilities across twelve states, Arizona, Connecticut, Iowa, Illinois, Kentucky, North Carolina, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Texas, Virginia, and Washington. As a KKR and GIP-owned private colocation operator, CyrusOne sits in this registry's colocation category alongside Digital Realty and QTS, leasing built data center capacity to enterprise and cloud tenants. Recent press coverage from late 2025 describes CyrusOne's private-equity-backed debt load as a factor in broader data center financing market volatility, though that reporting was not used here to source any operational fact about the company's facilities.
